findings.computation: Compare the article scale description with value labels V4225–V4247 in all three Form 4 dictionaries.
findings.notes: Article describes five categories; all supplied dictionaries describe four. This is a publication-versus-source-metadata contradiction, not a raw-data finding.

findings.computation: For a simple correlated five-factor covariance model with p indicators, free parameters are p+(p-5)+15=2p+10. p=19 gives 190-48=142 df per group, or 426 across three separate configural groups. Reported multigroup configural df is 375. p=18 would give 125 per group and 375 total; metric increment for 18 indicators with five markers would be 2*(18-5)=26, as printed.
findings.notes: This is conditional model-count algebra, not evidence authorizing an 18-item substitution. Unreported residual covariances, cross-loadings, constraints or model revisions could change df; original syntax is missing.

findings.check: Partial scalar footnotes versus df and anchor rule

inputs_locators.section_or_table: Table 2: scalar and partial scalar df
Primary Analyses: at least two invariant indicators

findings.computation: Six items have footnote a: two leisure, one intrinsic, one altruistic, two extrinsic. Releasing each intercept across all three groups would release 12 constraints, but scalar-to-partial df decreases by 427-417=10. Altruistic has two listed indicators and one is flagged, leaving one fully invariant indicator under a literal all-groups release interpretation.
findings.notes: Group-specific releases are not given. These are tensions in the documentation, not grounds to invent a release pattern or choose items from model fit.

findings.check: Metric-invariance nonsignificance claim versus chi-square statistic and df

inputs_locators.section_or_table: Primary Analyses: metric invariance described as ns

findings.computation: For chi-square difference 39.58 with 26 df, compute upper-tail probability across the complete statistic rounding interval.
findings.notes: The computed p is about .0429, contradicting ns at a conventional .05 threshold (the first star threshold in Table 2). A separately chosen stricter alpha could make ns true, but no such metric-test rule is reported. This does not contradict accepting metric invariance on the separate CFI criterion. The computed p is forensic only and is not inserted as a published exact_p target.
